bug_semantics: A backend user holding backend.manage_branding can store attacker-controlled LESS in Settings -> Customize Backend -> Styles. BrandSetting::compileCss() concatenates custom_css into the LESS input; LESS escape syntax such as ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>" preserves HTML delimiter and script text in the compiled result. BrandSetting::renderCss() returned that result without HTML sanitization, and modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php echoed it inside a <style> element on backend pages, so the stored </style> breakout executes script for backend viewers.
flaw_origin: Commit 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 first changed BrandSettings.php from parsing only the bundled custom.less file to parsing that file concatenated with self::get('custom_css'), while the compiled output was persisted/rendered without stripping HTML tags. The immediate parent already had the custom_css settings field and the style sink, but did not feed custom_css into the compiler, so this one-line data-flow addition is the smallest real BIC rather than later cache, rename, refactor, or error-handling commits.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 names human author Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com> and the same human committer, and its complete message is only 'Cache BrandSettings compiled CSS' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory GHSA-v7cf-8gh9-gxmj / CVE-2026-32257 identifies winter/wn-backend-module <=1.2.12 as affected, 1.2.13 as the first patched version, describes stored XSS through Brand Settings custom styles, and directly references https://github.com/wintercms/winter/commit/d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720.

git log -L over modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php history traces the vulnerable parser operand to 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 (2014-10-16, 'Cache BrandSettings compiled CSS'); later e7c33467f31c4a4a582ec82059735b32d1503f3b only split compilation into compileCss/cache plumbing, and later changes retained the same custom_css concatenation.

git show 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 shows the exact causal edit in modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php: $parser->parse(File::get(__DIR__.'/brandsettings/custom.less')) became $parser->parse(File::get(__DIR__.'/brandsettings/custom.less').self::get('custom_css')); the same commit wired rendered_css caching and did not sanitize compiled markup.

Direct parent-tree verification: git rev-parse 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74^ resolves fbaab26bfbcfef96bac4802fd6dd62ec5557c8e7. Reading that parent's modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php shows parser input only File::get(__DIR__.'/brandsettings/custom.less') and no self::get('custom_css'); reading the child shows the concatenation. Thus the vulnerable attacker-input-to-LESS data flow is absent from the immediate parent.

At tag v1.2.12, modules/backend/models/brandsetting/fields.yaml exposes custom_css as a LESS code editor; modules/backend/ServiceProvider.php gates the branding setting with backend.manage_branding; BrandSetting::compileCss() appends custom_css to LESS input; and modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php echoes BrandSetting::renderCss() unescaped inside <style>.

git show d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 changes BrandSetting::renderCss() from return $customCss to return strip_tags($customCss) and adds a regression payload using LESS escape syntax with </style><script>alert(1)</script><style>; its sole parent is 29f823bb21742e10b758c5d1dfdf7a1297688edf, so the advisory reference is itself the direct patch commit.

Version-boundary ancestry checks: v1.2.12 peels to b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313 and contains BIC 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 but not fix d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720; v1.2.13 resolves to e09c8d3526f3583cb6c3476a021b885088ecd4bd and contains the fix.

BIC-only AI inspection used git cat-file -p 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74. The commit object has one parent (not a squash aggregate), human author/committer Sam Georges, and no trailers or AI/bot markers. No fix, PR, branch, or later-commit signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 makes saved custom_css part of LESS compilation. Because LESS escape syntax can emit literal closing style and script markup, and the backend layout places renderCss() output directly inside a style element, a privileged branding editor can persist markup that executes for later backend viewers. History tracing separates the root-cause line from subsequent renames, cache refactors, exception handling, and the eventual sanitizer. The immediate parent retains the UI field and renderer but parses only trusted bundled LESS, proving absence of the exploitable data flow. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, so no squash decomposition is needed. The BIC predates and is contained by the last affected tag, while the advisory's direct sanitizer commit is absent from v1.2.12 and contained by v1.2.13. Finally, the BIC commit object is entirely human-authored/committed and contains no AI marker, which closes the attribution as NOT_AI.
